findings.quote: the 2024 spin-off of the Solventum health-care business and the completion of the company's exit from PFAS manufacturing by the end of that year
findings.issue: The only year named in the sentence is 2024 (the Solventum spin), so "by the end of that year" attaches the PFAS-manufacturing exit to end-2024. The grounding surface states the exit was completed at the end of 2025 (MD&A: "3M completed its exit of PFAS manufacturing by the end of 2025"; risk factors: "3M completed its exit of PFAS manufacturing at the end of 2025"), and every other section of this report dates it "end-2025" (thesis, catalysts, risks.idiosyncratic[0], durability). As written the overview misstates the completion year of a material corporate event and contradicts the rest of the report.
findings.fix: Replace "by the end of that year" with "by the end of 2025" so the PFAS-exit date matches the surface and the rest of the report; keep the 2024 date only for the Solventum spin-off.
findings.note: Addressed. companyOverview now reads "...the 2024 spin-off of the Solventum health-care business and the completion of the company's exit from PFAS manufacturing by the end of 2025." The PFAS-exit date is now end-2025, matching the MD&A ("completed its exit of PFAS manufacturing by the end of 2025") and the rest of the report; the 2024 date is retained only for the Solventum spin.

findings.quote: Transportation and Electronics is the higher-growth line, with sales of $2,066 million up 6.2 percent
findings.issue: The figures on the same page contradict the label. In Q2'26 Safety and Industrial grew faster than Transportation and Electronics on every measure the excerpt gives: total sales +8.2% vs +6.2%, organic +8.2% vs +5.9%, and for the six months +7.5% vs +4.1%. Two sentences earlier the report itself says Safety and Industrial "led on growth and profitability in Q2'26" at +8.2%, so calling T&E "the higher-growth line" at +6.2% in the adjacent sentence is internally inconsistent and unsupported by the series shown.
findings.fix: Drop "the higher-growth line." Characterise T&E by its actual drivers (semiconductor, aerospace, data center) without ranking it above Safety and Industrial on growth, or move any "higher-growth" framing to a secular/end-market claim explicitly distinct from the Q2 print if the surface supports it.
findings.note: Addressed. "the higher-growth line" is gone. Moat body now reads "Transportation and Electronics grew 6.2 percent to sales of $2,066 million, with operating income of $503 million at a 24.4 percent margin, driven by strength in semiconductor, aerospace and data center demand," with no growth-ranking above Safety and Industrial. All figures ($2,066M, +6.2%, $503M, 24.4%) match the MD&A.

findings.quote: The Consumer segment is contracting, with management citing weak consumer and consumer-electronics demand, which offsets part of the industrial recovery.
findings.issue: The surface supports "weakness," not an asserted absolute decline. The MD&A says total sales growth was "partially offset by weakness in consumer/consumer electronics" and cites "weakness in auto and consumer electronics"; no Consumer segment sales figure is captured (the report elsewhere admits "the interim excerpt gives no standalone Consumer figure"). Asserting the segment is "contracting"/"shrinking" is an inference the source invites but does not make and would require a residual computation the author is barred from doing. Same overreach recurs in sections.businessMoat.durability ("the Consumer segment is shrinking"). The softer growth.points[4] phrasing ("a drag on growth") is fine.
findings.fix: Soften "contracting"/"shrinking" to "weak" or "a drag," matching the MD&A's "weakness" language, unless a Consumer segment figure showing an absolute decline is added to the grounding surface.
findings.note: Addressed. risks.idiosyncratic[4] now reads "Consumer demand is weak, with management citing weakness in consumer and consumer-electronics markets..." The durability recurrence is softened to "Consumer demand is soft," and the moat body says "The Consumer line is soft." No "contracting"/"shrinking" remains; all Consumer references now use the MD&A's "weakness"/"soft"/"drag" language.

findings.quote: Q2'26 organic sales grew 2.3 percent and the adjusted operating margin reached 24.9 percent
findings.issue: This is a near-verbatim paraphrase of the thesis (sections.executiveSummary.thesis.body: "Q2'26 organic sales rose 2.3 percent and the adjusted operating margin was 24.9 percent"), the same claim made twice in different words in two sections. The pattern recurs with other figures: the 19.0x next-twelve-month multiple is restated as a number in thesis, valuation.multiplesCommentary and finalRecommendation.body[0]; the $1.4B / 5.6% FY25 free cash flow appears as a figure in thesis, financials.cashflowCommentary, risks.idiosyncratic[1] and finalRecommendation.body[1]; and the "$4.7 billion equity / thin cushion" claim appears in financials.balanceCommentary, executiveSummary.risks[4] and risks.idiosyncratic[2]. House style asks that each figure be introduced once per section and referred back in words, with the executive summary and final recommendation pointing rather than restating.
findings.fix: In the finalRecommendation, refer back to the Q2'26 recovery in words rather than re-quoting 2.3% and 24.9%; likewise state the 19.0x multiple and the $1.4B/5.6% FCF as figures once (in valuation and cashflow respectively) and refer back in words in the exec summary and final recommendation.
findings.note: Addressed. finalRecommendation.body[0] now refers to the recovery in words ("organic sales turned higher in Q2'26 and adjusted operating margins expanded"), not 2.3%/24.9%. The 19.0x multiple now appears as a figure only in valuation.multiplesCommentary (thesis and finalRec use words); $1.4B/5.6% FCF only in cashflowCommentary (thesis, idiosyncratic[1], finalRec.body[1] use words); $4.7B equity only in balanceCommentary (exec risks[4], idiosyncratic[2] use words). Each figure now once per section.

findings.quote: Governance rests on the DEF 14A proxy statement, filed 2026-03-25, which is included in our pack.
findings.issue: Date is written in ISO form (2026-03-25) in prose; house style requires prose-form dates. The insiderOwnership section, by contrast, correctly uses prose form ("December 31, 2023").
findings.fix: Write the date in prose form, e.g. "filed March 25, 2026."
findings.note: Addressed. governance now reads "Governance rests on the DEF 14A proxy statement, filed March 25, 2026, which is included in our pack." Date is in prose form.

findings.quote: Q2'26 net sales were $6,500 million, up 2.4 percent, with organic sales up 2.3 percent.
findings.issue: The grounding surface carries two figures for Q2'26 YoY revenue growth: the MD&A's "Total sales change 2.4%" and the vendor Trailing-twelve-months block's "revenue +2.5% YoY" (the snapshot shows +2% rounded to 0dp). The report uses 2.4% here and in analystCommentary without noting the vendor's 2.5%. Per the source-disagreement rule the report should say which figure it used. The difference is immaterial (0.1pp) and 2.4% is the authoritative filing figure, so this is Minor.
findings.fix: Optionally add a half-clause noting the vendor shows +2.5% and that the report uses the filing's 2.4% GAAP total-sales-change figure; or leave as-is given the difference is rounding-level.
findings.note: Addressed. incomeCommentary now states the disagreement once: "up 2.4 percent on the filing's total-sales-change basis — the vendor snapshot shows +2.5 percent, and we use the filing figure." The note appears only here, not repeated in analystCommentary, satisfying the source-disagreement rule (said once, states which figure used).
